neighbours.label: the period that ends an instruction or step in procedural text
fire: Unplug the router before you open the case. Then remove the four screws.
Make sure the oven is fully preheated. Place the tray on the middle rack.
Write the total cost of the items on the form. Hand it to the clerk.
Check that the backup has finished. Restart the server afterwards.
Let the paint dry overnight before the second coat. Sand it lightly.
Ask the students to read the passage aloud. Discuss the main idea.
Measure the distance between the two posts. Cut the board to length.
Confirm that the tank is empty before cleaning. Rinse it with water.
quiet: The router sat on a shelf near the window and blinked all night
The oven in our old flat was small and never got very hot
The clerk at the counter wore a green sweater and smiled at everyone
The server room was cold and noisy on that winter morning
The paint on the fence was a pale yellow that faded in the sun
The students in the back row were laughing at a joke
The two posts at the end of the garden leaned to the left
The tank behind the barn was rusty and covered with moss

notes: Card/look: mostly ',' and '.' at clause ends, often in how-to text (pay for the shares., accept the new kernel., talk you out of taking drugs.) and Russian. Probe was mixed: 0.31-0.38 on two instruction periods, 0.09 on another. Likely to fail.
